en: Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa,
Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa, Hare Hare;
Hare Rāma, Hare Rāma.
Rāma, Rāma! Hare, Hare!
Worship Govinda, worship Govinda,
O dull-witted one, worship Govinda now that the appointed time has arrived!
No, no; [the root] *ḍukṛñ* means "to do" (*karaṇe*). || 1 ||
O fool, abandon the thirst for the acquisition of wealth; cultivate right understanding in your mind and be free from craving.
Accept whatever you obtain through the results of your own past actions.
With that wealth, dispel the mind's distress. || 2 ||
Upon seeing the weight of a woman's breasts and the region of her navel, do not fall under the sway of delusion;
for this is merely a transformation of flesh, fat, and the like.
Contemplate this in your mind again and again. 3.
Know that life is exceedingly fickle, like a drop of water on a lotus leaf,
seized by disease and pride.
And the entire world, stricken with grief. || 4 ||
As long as one is intent on acquiring wealth, one's own circle remains devoted;
afterwards, when the body has grown decrepit, they remain behind.
No one at all asks for news in the house. || 5 ||
As long as the vital breath dwells within the body,
one inquires after the welfare of the household; but when the breath has departed and the body is gone, [who would ask]?
Wives are afraid of that body. || 6 ||
The child is attached to play;
the youth is attached to young women;
the old man is attached to anxiety.
No one at all is attached to the supreme Brahman. || 7 ||
Who is your beloved? Who is your son?
This saṃsāra is exceedingly diverse.
To whom do you belong, who are you, and from where have you come?
Therefore, O brother, contemplate that reality here. 8.
In the state of association with the virtuous, there is freedom from attachment; in freedom from attachment, freedom from delusion;
and in freedom from delusion, the immovable reality.
In the state of unwavering reality lies liberation while living (jīvanmukti). 9.
When youth has passed, what transformation of passion remains?
When the water is dried up, what lake remains?
When wealth is exhausted, what retinue remains?
When reality is known, what is saṃsāra? 10.
Do not harbor pride regarding wealth, kin, or youth;
time takes away everything in the blink of an eye.
Abandoning all this which is composed of illusion, [seek the truth].
Having understood it, enter the state of Brahman. 11.
Day and night, evening and morning,
winter and spring return again;
time plays on, while life passes away.
Yet even that is not released by the wind of hope. 12.
This entire instruction for the grammarian has indeed been told by the twelve Mañjarikās,
who are experts in the knowledge of the earth.
By those who have taken refuge in the venerable Lord Śaṅkara. 12a.
O madman, when your beloved has been won and your anxiety regarding wealth has vanished, do you have no restrainer?
In the three worlds, the company of the virtuous is the only one.
It is a boat for crossing the ocean of existence. 13.
Though he has matted hair, a shaven head, or plucked-out locks,
and though he is dressed in many saffron garments,
the fool does not see even while seeing.
One who frequently changes his dress for the sake of deception regarding his belly. 14.
The limbs have wasted away, the head is grey and shaven, the teeth are gone, and the beard is matted;
the old man walks along, leaning upon a staff.
Even so, it does not relinquish its lump of hope. 15.
With fire before him and the sun behind, resting his knees upon his chin at night,
subsisting on alms in the palms of his hands, he dwells beneath the shade of trees.
Even then, the noose of hope does not release him. || 16 ||
One devoid of knowledge performs the journey to the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean, or the observance of vows, or the giving of gifts— according to every opinion.
One does not attain liberation even in a hundred births. ॥ 17॥
Dwelling in temples or at the foot of trees,
with the ground for a bed and deerskin for clothing,
he has renounced all possessions and enjoyments.
To whom does dispassion not bring happiness? || 18 ||
Whether devoted to yoga, or devoted to worldly enjoyment, or devoted to attachment, or free from attachment— for him whose mind delights in Brahman, [there is no difference].
He rejoices, he rejoices, he indeed rejoices. 19.
By whomsoever even a little of the Bhagavad Gītā has been studied, a single drop of the water of the Gaṅgā drunk,
or even once the worship of Murāri performed—
Yama does not even consider making an inquiry into his case. || 20 ||
Again birth, again death,
again lying within the womb of a mother—
in this saṃsāra so difficult to cross.
Out of compassion, O Murāri, protect me in this shoreless [ocean]. 21.
Wearing a patched garment made from the streets,
following a path devoid of merit and demerit,
the yogi has his mind fixed in yoga.
He delights like a child or a madman. 22.
"Who are you? Who am I? From where have I come?
Who is my mother? Who is my father?"—reflect thus upon everything as being without essence.
Having abandoned all investigation into dreams and the universe. 23.
Whether in you, in me, or elsewhere, Viṣṇu is one and the same; why do you, being intolerant, bearlessly become angry with me? Be equanimous toward all.
If you desire the state of Viṣṇu before long... 24.
Exert no effort in making war or peace toward enemy, friend, son, or kinsman; rather,
look upon yourself in everyone.
Abandon the ignorance of duality everywhere. 25.
Having abandoned desire, anger, greed, and delusion, contemplate the Self, asking "Who am I?
Fools are those devoid of self-knowledge.
They are cooked, hidden away in hell. 26.
The Gītā by name is to be sung;
the form of the Lord of Śrī is to be meditated upon incessantly;
the mind is to be led toward the company of the virtuous.
And wealth should be given to the poor. 27.
One indulges in the enjoyment of women for the sake of pleasure, only for disease to arise in the body afterwards;
alas, even though death is the refuge in this world!
Even so, he does not abandon his practice of evil. || 28 ||
Constantly contemplate wealth as a calamity;
therefore, it is true that not even a fraction of happiness exists therein.
Even from one's own son, those who possess wealth experience fear.
This rule is established everywhere. 29.
Breath control (prāṇāyāma), withdrawal of the senses (pratyāhāra),
discernment through the distinction between the eternal and the non-eternal,
and the practice of meditative absorption (samādhi) accompanied by the recitation of mantras (jāpya).
"Exert great attention; pay close heed. (30)
O you who possess intense devotion for the lotus feet of the Guru,
you shall soon be liberated from saṃsāra through the very restraint of the senses and the mind.
You shall behold the God residing within your own heart. 31.
A certain foolish grammarian,
preeminent in the study of the root *ḍukṛñ* (to do/make),
[was] a disciple of the venerable Śrī Śaṅkarabhagavat.
Awakened and having purified his faculties. 32.
Worship Govinda, worship Govinda,
O dull-witted one, worship Govinda;
there is no other means than the remembrance of His name.
For we do not see you as one who has crossed over. 33.
